QASHANI:92:8-12/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:8-12/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:8-12/r4.claim: Wealth cannot help its owner after the person falls into hell’s well and the depth of the abyss.
QASHANI:92:8-12/r4.anchor: إذا وقع في قعر بئر جهنم وعمق الهاوية وهلك

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.claim: Verses 11–14 admonish Quraysh that God guides through revelation but does not force acceptance; they alone benefit from accepting, while both worlds remain under His control.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.anchor: this world and the next are in the grasp of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r3.claim: Mā in verse 11 may be negative or interrogative; Islahi prefers the interrogative reading because it adds emphasis.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r3.anchor: an emphasis shall be added to the verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r4.claim: The wealthy are warned that wealth benefits them permanently only when spent for God and preserved for eternal life; otherwise it becomes a source of doom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r4.anchor: spending it for the cause of God

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p377#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p377#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p377#3/r1.claim: Qatada explains plunging as plunging into the Fire.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p377#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا تردى ﴾ قال إذا تردى في النار

QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r12.claim: Wealth cannot benefit its owner when he dies.
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r12.anchor: وما يغنى عنه ماله إذا تردى

TUSTARI:92:10-11/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:10-11/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:10-11/r1.claim: God makes the hard path easy by enabling the person to perform the deeds of Hell; his wealth cannot help when he falls into it.
TUSTARI:92:10-11/r1.anchor: أي نسهل عليه العمل، بعمل أهل النار، ألا تراه كيف قال عقبه:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r4.claim: Mā in ما يغني can be negative or interrogative, asking what wealth could avail him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r4.anchor: وما يغني: يجوز أن تكون ما نافية واستفهامية، أي: وأي شيء يغني عنه ماله؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r5.anchor: وإذا تردى: تفعل من الردى، أي هلك، قاله مجاهد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r6.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r6.claim: Qatada and Abū Ṣāliḥ say taraddā means falling into Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح: تردى في جهنم: أي سقط من حافاتها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r7.claim: Other interpreters say it means being shrouded in burial clothes; two poetic citations use ridāʾ in this death-related sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r7.anchor: وقال قوم: تردى بأكفانه، من الردى، وقال مالك بن الذئب:

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r1.claim: The first clause says his wealth will not benefit him; alternatively, mā is an interrogative asking what could benefit him. Taradda means death, falling into the grave or Hell, or being wrapped in a shroud as a euphemism for death.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r1.anchor: أي ولا يغني عنه على أن ما نافية أو أي شيء يغني عنه ماله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r2.claim: Mujahid explains taradda as perishing, from the word for destruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r2.anchor: تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك قاله مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains taradda as falling into the grave.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r4.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r4.claim: Qatada and Abu Salih explain it as falling into Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#4/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح تردى في جهنم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the miser’s wealth will not benefit him when he dies; Qatada and Abu Salih say when he falls into Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r1.anchor: {وما يغني عنه ماله} الذي بخل به، {إذا تردى} قال مجاهد: إذا مات.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r4.claim: His wealth will not help when he perishes, falls into a grave, or drops into Hell; ما يغني can be a plain negation or a rhetorical question.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r4.anchor: { وما يغنى عنه ماله } نفي أو استفهام إنكار. { إذا تردى } هلك تفعل من الردى

BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.claim: The contrast concerns giving away wealth and hoarding it: the passage says the miser's wealth will not help him and describes the giver as giving wealth to purify himself.
BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1.anchor: وإنه لكذلك، الإعطاء للمال والبخل به، في آيتي الليل

BINTSHATI:v2p109/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r3.claim: Ghina can mean self-sufficiency even without wealth, while thara denotes possession of wealth unless used figuratively.
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r3.anchor: الفرق بين الغنى والثراء، إذ يغلب أن يكون الغنى غنى النفس

BINTSHATI:v2p109/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r4.claim: Rada originally means destruction and includes the physical image of a rock or falling into a well, then extends to ruin generally.
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r4.anchor: وتردى في البئر سقط، ثم استعمل في مطلق الهلاك

BINTSHATI:v2p110/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r1.claim: Taradda is the intransitive form of arda, to destroy or cause ruin; the Quran uses the root in related forms for perishing, causing ruin, and a fallen animal, and this exhausts its occurrences.
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r1.anchor: وهذا هو كل ما في القرآن من المادة

BINTSHATI:v2p110/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r2.claim: The author understands taradda as plunging into ruin and prefers al-Tabari's reading as falling into Hell over the reported burial-shroud reading.
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r2.anchor: أقرب إلى المعنى والسياق من قول قوم

BINTSHATI:v2p110/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan transmits the alternative reading of taradda as being covered by a burial shroud, supported by lines from Malik ibn al-Rayb and another poet.
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r3.anchor: من قول قوم، فيما نقل أبو حيان

BINTSHATI:v2p110/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r4.claim: The shroud reading does not fit the warning against the miser, since death in a shroud applies to believers as well as disbelievers.
BINTSHATI:v2p110/r4.anchor: لأن التردى برداء الكفن لا يختص به كافر دون مؤمن

BINTSHATI:v2p111/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p111/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p111/r5.claim: The author prefers the negative parsing of ma because it emphatically states that wealth cannot help the miser when he falls into ruin.
BINTSHATI:v2p111/r5.anchor: والنفي عندنا أولى، لما فيه من ملحظ التقرير لعدم غنى المال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r1.claim: The miser’s wealth cannot save him when he falls into the grave or Hell; the verb can signify ruin or falling into a pit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r1.anchor: أي هلك بالسقوط في حفرة القبر والنار , تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك والسقوط في بئر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r2.claim: The opening may be read as a rhetorical question, which denies the wealth’s benefit emphatically.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استفهاما إنكاريا فيكون نافيا للإغناء على أبلغ وجه

NAHHAS:v5p241/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p241/r16.claim: Mā is the direct object of yughni; no wealth can protect him when he falls into the Fire. Mujāhid takes taraddā as perishing; the root can also mean falling.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r16.anchor: ما في موضع نصب بيغني أي وأي شيء يدفع عنه ماله إذا سقط في النار وذهب مجاهد إذا هلك وإنما يقال في الهلاك ردى يردي وتردى إذا سقط

NAHHAS:v5p241/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p241/r17.claim: The separate root rādiʾa means to be base or defective, as in rādiʾ/murdīʾ.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r17.anchor: وردؤ الرجل يردؤ رداءة وهو رديء مردىء

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r7.claim: He glossed falling as falling into the Fire and said the verse was revealed about Abu Jahl.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r7.anchor: وأخرج الطستي في مسائله عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r1.speaker: عدي بن زيد
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r1.claim: His poem uses تردى for being overtaken by death and brought down while still hoping for a long life, supporting the Arabic word's sense.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r1.anchor: أما سمعت قول عدي بن زيد: خطفته منية

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r2.claim: He glossed falling as entering the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r2.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r3.speaker: غير مسمى في النص
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r3.claim: An unattributed gloss says wealth will not avail the person when he falls into the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة {وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى}

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r4.claim: He glossed falling as dying and the blazing fire as one that flares up.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r4.anchor: وأخرج الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1.claim: The preceding surah swore by the soul's shaping, meaning the creation of intellect and knowledge; this surah swears by the human body and its sexes. The oath's response is that human efforts differ, with the emphasis on wealth failing in the fall.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1.anchor: وقد كان القسم في سورة الشمس بتسوية النفس ، أي خلق العقل والمعرفة في الإنسان ، وأما القسم هنا فبخلق جسد الإنسان واختلاف صنفيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2.claim: سعي literally means brisk, forceful walking and is metaphorically used for work and striving.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2.anchor: والسعي حقيقته : المشي القوي الحثيث ، وهو مستعار هنا للعمل والكد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r4.claim: Verse 11 coordinates with the preceding promise: wealth withheld will not help when its owner falls into Hell; تردى means falling from a height to a depth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r4.anchor: وجملة : { وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى } عطف على جملة { فسنيسره للعسرى } أي سنعجل به إلى جهنم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r5.claim: ما may be a negation or a rhetorical question of rebuke; on the latter reading, the waw can introduce a new sentence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r5.anchor: و { ما } يجوز أن تكون نافية . والتقدير : وسوف لا يغني عنه ماله إذا سقط في جهنم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r4.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r4.claim: Qatada and Abu Salih say taradda means falling into Hell from its edges.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r4.anchor: فقال قتادة وأبو صالح معناه تردى في جهنم، أي سقط من حافاتها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says taradda means perished, from the word for ruin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تردى معناه هلك من الردى،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r6.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r6.claim: Others interpret it as wrapping himself in a burial shroud, supported by two poems.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r6.anchor: وقال قوم معناه تردى بأكفانه من الرداء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#4/r1.claim: The wealth a person withheld will not help when they fall into Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#4/r1.anchor: إذا تردى في جهنم قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والمعنى إذا سقط فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#4/r2.claim: Alternatively, it will not help when the person dies and falls into the grave.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#4/r2.anchor: إذا مات فتردى في قبره قاله مجاهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets the miser's downfall as death.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421/r2.claim: Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam interpret the downfall as falling into the Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421/r2.anchor: وقال أبو صالح، ومالك عن زيد بن أسلم: إذا تردى في النار.

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r9.claim: Taraddī can mean falling from a height or being destroyed, from al-radā.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r9.anchor: والتردي: السقوط من علو إلى سفل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r4.claim: ما يغني عنه is either a rhetorical question rejecting any benefit from his wealth or a plain negation; تردى can mean death, falling into a grave, or plunging into Hell's depth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r4.anchor: { وما يغنى عنه } استفهام في معنى الإنكار . أو نفي { تردى } تفعل من الردى

SAMIN-DURR:92:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:11/r1.claim: ‘Ma’ may be a simple negation (‘his wealth will not benefit him’) or a rhetorical, denying question.
SAMIN-DURR:92:11/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون " ما " نفيا، وأن تكون استفهاما إنكاريا

SAMIN-DURR:92:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:11/r2.claim: ‘Taradda’ may mean perishing, or being wrapped in a shroud, a euphemism for death; two poems use the shroud sense.
SAMIN-DURR:92:11/r2.anchor: تردى } إما من الهلاك، أو من تردى بأكفانه، وهو كناية عن الموت

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r39.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r39.speaker: أبو صالح، زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r39.claim: Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam say the person falls into the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r39.anchor: إذا تردى في النار , قاله أبو صالح وزيد بن أسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r40.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r40.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r40.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say the person dies and falls into his grave.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r40.anchor: إذا مات فتردى في قبره , قاله مجاهد وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r41.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r41.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r41.claim: Mawardi also allows a fall into misguidance and disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r41.anchor: إذا تردى في ضلاله وهوى في معاصيه

MUJAHID:v2p765#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p765#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p765#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the person cannot benefit from wealth when he dies.
MUJAHID:v2p765#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى ﴾ يعني إذا مات

MUQATIL:92:7-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:92:7-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:92:7-15/r3.claim: Abu Sufyan's hoarded money will not help when he dies and falls into the Fire.
MUQATIL:92:7-15/r3.anchor: { وما يغني عنه ماله } الذي بخل به في الدنيا { إذا تردى } [آية: 11] يعني إذا مات

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r1.claim: His wealth will not benefit him when he perishes; taradda derives from destruction.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r1.anchor: ولم ينفع ماله إذا هلك وتردى تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r2.claim: Alternatively, taradda means falling into the grave.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r2.anchor: أ وتردى فى القبر أ وفى قعر جهنم أى سقط

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r3.claim: Alternatively, taradda means falling into the depths of Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#12/r3.anchor: أ وتردى فى القبر أ وفى قعر جهنم أى سقط

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r1.claim: Tarrada can mean that the man died or perished; a poetic line illustrates the language of destruction.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r1.anchor: إذا تردى } أي مات. يقال: ردي الرجل يردى ردى: إذا هلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r2.speaker: أبو صالح وزيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r2.claim: Abu Salih and Zayd ibn Aslam take tarrada as falling into Hell, linked to the word for one who falls to death.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r2.anchor: وقال أبو صالح وزيد بن أسلم: «إذا تردى»: سقط في جهنم ومنه المتردية.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r3.claim: The verb also describes falling into a well or plunging from a mountain; the idiom can ask where someone went.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r3.anchor: ويقال: ردي في البئر وتردى: إذا سقط في بئر، أو تهور من جبل.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r4.claim: Ma may be a negation, meaning his wealth helps him nothing, or a rebuking question asking what it could do after his fall.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r4.anchor: و«ما»: يحتمل أن تكون جحدا أي ولا يغني عنه ماله شيئا ويحتمل أن تكون استفهاما

QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r1.claim: At the end of repeated stumbles and deviations, wealth hoarded or used to replace God and guidance cannot help its owner.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r1.anchor: فإذا تردى وسقط في نهاية العثرات والانحرافات لم يغن عنه ماله الذي بخل به

QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r2.claim: Being enabled in sin is the hard path even if its owner prospers in this world; nothing is harder than Hell, which is the ultimate hardship.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r2.anchor: والتيسير للشر والمعصية من التيسير للعسرى ، وإن أفلح صاحبها في هذه الأرض

QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r3.claim: Across all times and places there are two paths, parties, and standards beneath many outward forms; each person chooses, and God facilitates that chosen route.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r3.anchor: وقد تبين طريقان ونهجان للجموع البشرية في كل زمان ومكان

QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r4.claim: The next section describes each group’s end and first establishes that each outcome is just, true, and inevitable.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r4.anchor: وقبل كل شيء يقرر أن ما يلاقيه كل فريق من عاقبة ومن جزاء هو عدل وحق

RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r1.claim: The particle ما can be either a rhetorical question of denial or a plain negation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r1.anchor: ما هنا يحتمل أن يكون استفهاما

RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r2.claim: One reading of تردى derives it from falling: the miser falls into the grave or Hell, where the wealth he left heirs cannot help him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r2.anchor: أن يكون ذلك مأخوذا من قولك

RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r3.claim: The wealth left behind does not accompany its owner; only charitable deeds and wealth spent in its proper rights benefit him in the next life.

RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r4.claim: Alternatively, تردى is derived from destruction and means death.
RAZI-FULL:v31p183/r4.anchor: أن تردى تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك يريد الموت

STUDYQURAN:92:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:11/r1.claim: The clause may instead be rendered as a rhetorical question asking what wealth will avail when its owner perishes.
STUDYQURAN:92:11/r1.anchor: Alternately, “What will his wealth avail him when he perishes?”

STUDYQURAN:92:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:11/r2.speaker: IK and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:92:11/r2.claim: “Perishes” may refer either to dying or to entering the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:92:11/r2.anchor: Perishes can be taken to mean when he dies or when he enters the Fire (IK, Ṭ).

ASAD-NOTES:92:8#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:92:8#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:92:8#n6/r1.claim: The phrase may be rendered as a statement: his wealth will be of no avail when he falls.
ASAD-NOTES:92:8#n6/r1.anchor: Or (as a statement): "of no avail will be to him his wealth when he..."

TAB:92:11/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:11/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:11/r1.claim: The miser's wealth cannot protect him on the Day of Resurrection when he falls into ruin.
TAB:92:11/r1.anchor: أيّ شيء يدفع عن هذا الذي بخل بماله ،   واستغنى عن ربه ،   مالُه يوم القيامة إذَا هو تَرَدّى ؟

TAB:92:11/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:11/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:92:11/r2.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ interprets the fall as falling into Hell.
TAB:92:11/r2.anchor: عن أبي صالح وَما يُغْني عَنْهُ مالُهُ إذَا تَرَدّى قال :  في جهنم

TAB:92:11/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:11/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:11/r3.claim: Qatāda likewise says the person falls into the Fire.
TAB:92:11/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  إذَا تَرَدّى قال :  إذا تردّى في النار

TAB:92:11/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:11/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:92:11/r4.claim: Mujāhid instead interprets the fall as death.
TAB:92:11/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد وَما يُغْني عَنْهُ مالُهُ إذَا تَرَدّى قال :  إذا مات

TAB:92:11/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:11/r5.speaker: author
TAB:92:11/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers falling into Hell, the usual meaning of تردّى; the verb for dying is ردي, and تردّى is rarely used for death.
TAB:92:11/r5.anchor: وأَولَى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال :  معناه :  إذا تردّى في جهنم ،   لأن ذلك هو المعروف من التردّي

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Bergsträßer
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r1.claim: Mā can be read either as a question pronoun or as a negation particle.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Mā kann sowohl Fragepronomen („Was hilft ihm sein Besitz?“) wie auch Verneinungspartikel („Sein Besitz hilft ihm nicht“) sein (Bergsträßer 1914, 29)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r2.claim: The negation is more likely here; the commentary points to 111:2 and two biblical intertexts.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r2.anchor: wahrscheinlicher ist hier letzteres. S. die Anmerkung zu 111:2 mit zwei biblischen Intertexten

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.claim: Neuwirth classifies verse 11 with the theological predication in verses 12–13 rather than with the preceding description of the wicked.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.anchor: anders Neuwirth, Studien, 229 und Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 228

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r7.claim: Verse 11 belongs with the wicked person's section because its pronoun points back to him, its root ġ-n-y echoes verse 8, and inna marks a fresh start at verse 12; it creates an asymmetry.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r7.anchor: Der Vers bezieht sich pronominal auf den Bösen zurück und ist lexikalisch mit V. 8 verknüpft (mā yuġnī ʿanhū, „ihm hilft nicht …“, enthält dieselbe Wurzel ġ-n-y wie istaġnā aus V. 8)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

TABATABAI:92:8-13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r3.claim: Tarradda is falling from a height and by extension destruction; the fall may be into the grave, Hell, or simply death. The question asks what his wealth could do, or states that it will do nothing.
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r3.anchor: التردي هو السقوط من مكان عال ويطلق على الهلاك

TABRISI:92:5-15/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r12.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:92:5-15/r12.claim: Wealth cannot help its owner when he falls into the Fire; Mujahid says the fall may mean death and destruction.
TABRISI:92:5-15/r12.anchor: أي سقط في النار عن قتادة وأبي صالح

THALABI:v10p217/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي
THALABI:v10p217/r9.claim: At a funeral the Prophet says each person has a written place in Paradise and a place in Hell; a man asks whether they should then rely on the writing.
THALABI:v10p217/r9.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان في جنازة فأخذ عودا

THALABI:v10p218/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p218/r1.claim: In response to the question about relying on one's written fate, the Prophet says to act, since each person is facilitated toward their outcome, then recites the passage about giving and withholding.
THALABI:v10p218/r1.anchor: فقال «اعملوا فكل ميسر» ، ثم قرأ فأما من أعطى واتقى الآيات

THALABI:v10p218/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218/r3.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
THALABI:v10p218/r3.claim: They interpret the fall as a pit in Hell.
THALABI:v10p218/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح: هو لحد في جهنم

THALABI:v10p218/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218/r4.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v10p218/r4.claim: He says the verse was revealed about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
THALABI:v10p218/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: نزلت في أبي سفيان بن حرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r1.claim: His wealth will not help when he dies; the wealth meant is what he withheld from good works.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r1.anchor: {وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى} (¬3) أي الذي بخل به عن الخير. {إذا تردى} إذا مات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r2.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل وأبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r2.claim: They interpret taradda as dying; Abu ʿUbayda glosses it as perishing, and al-Mubarrad derives it from destruction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد (¬4)، ومقاتل، (وأبو صالح (¬5)) (¬6): قال أبو عبيدة (¬7): "تردى" وردى إذا مات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r3.claim: They interpret the phrase as falling into Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬9)، وقتادة (¬10): إذا تردى في جهنم، أي سقط # وهوى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r4.claim: He points to the term al-mutardiya as another use of the same word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p82/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬9)، وقتادة (¬10): إذا تردى في جهنم، أي سقط # وهوى، وذكرنا هذا الحرف عند قوله: {والمتردية} (¬1)

WAHIDI-QT:92:11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:11/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:11/r1.claim: One gloss takes taradda to mean that he died and perished.

WAHIDI-QT:92:11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:11/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:11/r2.claim: Another gloss says he fell into Hell.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:10-19/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:10-19/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:10-19/r2.claim: Wealth cannot benefit a person when he dies and perishes; another interpretation says when he falls into Hell.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:10-19/r2.anchor: { وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى } أي: مات وهلك. وقيل: سقط في جهنم.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p374/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p374/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p374/r1.claim: ما يغني عنه ماله can be both a reproachful question and a negation: the wording intentionally asks what his wealth can avail and states that it will not avail him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p374/r1.anchor: جاء سبحانه وتعالى بلفظ يتسع للمعنيين وهو يريدهما معا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r1.claim: The broad wording ولا تشركوا به شيئا can forbid both any object of association and any degree of shirk, whereas أحدا in the other verse specifies the meaning; كثيرا likewise allows several readings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r1.anchor: تحتمل المعنيين والمراد منها أن لا نشرك بالله شيئا من الشرك أو شيئا من الأشياء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r2.claim: إذا is used for events known to happen or to recur: death, the end of sacred months, sunrise, and the completion of prayer are certain examples.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r1.claim: When إذا and إن occur together, إذا marks the more frequent event and إن the less frequent one; across the Qur'an إذا introduces certain or common events, while إن can mark hypothetical, rare, doubtful, or impossible ones.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r1.anchor: وإذا جاءت (إذا) و (إن) في نفس الآية تدل (إذا) على الكثير و (إن) على الأقل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r2.claim: Tumbling into death, destruction, the grave, or Hell is certain, so if cannot replace إذا; the certainty warns misers and tyrants that wealth cannot save them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r2.anchor: والتردي حاصل والتردي إما أن يكون من الموت أو الهلاك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.claim: The lām emphasizing God's ownership suits the surah's repeated focus on wealth and possession; unlike this context, the wealth-free context of 53:25 omits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.anchor: فسياق الآيات في سورة الليل جاء كله في الأموال وامتلاكها والتصرف فيها

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r9.claim: When he falls into the pit, dies, or is destroyed, his wealth cannot rescue him from the grave or ruin and instead increases his punishment and loss.
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r9.anchor: Kıyıp veremeyerek topladığı ve onunla zengin olmak, müstağnî kalmak istediği mal onu kabre yuvarlanmaktan, helâk ile esfel-i sâfilîne gitmekten kurtaracak değil

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r10.claim: Teraddā may derive from radā, meaning destruction, or from taraddud, meaning to roll or fall; on the latter analysis its original form is taraddada.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4.claim: Left to himself, a person pursues desire without regard to lawful limits, finds sin easy and pleasurable, ends in Hell, and cannot ransom himself with accumulated wealth (5:36; 70:11–16).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4.anchor: kendi başına kalan kul helâl haram demeden nefsânî arzularını tatmine çalışır; kötülük yapmak, günah işlemek ona kolay gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

FARRA:v3p271/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p271/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p271/r2.claim: Fasanuyassiruhu means “We will prepare him”; Arabic also says yassarat al-ghanam when sheep are ready to give birth.
FARRA:v3p271/r2.anchor: وجل: فسنيسره سنهيئه. والعرب تقول: قد يسرت الغنم إذا ولدت وتهيأت للولادة:

FARRA:v3p271/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p271/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p271/r3.claim: A poet’s line “our two masters … when their sheep are ready” attests yassarat in the sense of readiness for lambing.
FARRA:v3p271/r3.anchor:
وتهيأت للولادة: وقال الشاعر :
هما سيدانا يزعمان وإنما ... يسوداننا أن يسرت غنماهما

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

TAB-FULL:v24p474/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r1.speaker: ابو صالح
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r1.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ interprets the miser's downfall as falling into Hell.
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي خالد، عن أبي صالح، {وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى} [الليل: 11] قال: في جهنم

TAB-FULL:v24p474/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r2.claim: Qatāda also says the man falls into the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إذا تردى} [الليل: 11] قال: إذا تردى في النار

TAB-FULL:v24p474/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r3.claim: Mujāhid interprets the downfall as death.
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r3.anchor: عن ليث، عن مجاهد، {وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى} [الليل: 11] قال: إذا مات

TAB-FULL:v24p474/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r4.claim: Ṭabarī prefers falling into Hell because that is the established sense of taraddā; death is usually expressed by radā, and taraddā is rarely used for it.
TAB-FULL:v24p474/r4.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: معناه: إذا تردى في جهنم، لأن ذلك هو المعروف من التردي

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r4.claim: His wealth cannot help him when he dies.
THALABI:v10p220/r4.anchor: وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى يعني به إذا مات

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r1.claim: The first line about the two women is low in information and lacks beauty, showing that polished wording can still be empty of meaning.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r1.anchor: أنت لا تشك في أن البيت الأول قليل الفائدة ليس له مع ذلك بهجة فقد يكون الكلام مصنوع اللفظ وإن كان منزوع المعنى

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r2.claim: Saying their scent appears only when they stand is a limitation; an improved line would say they are fragrant in every state.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r2.anchor: ولو أراد أن يجود أفاد أن بهما طيبا على كل حال فأما في حال القيام فقط فذلك تقصير

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r3.claim: After comparing their scent to musk, the poet weakens the image by comparing it again to a breeze carrying clove’s fragrance.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r3.anchor: ثم فيه خلل آخر لأنه بعد أن شبه عرفها بالمسك شبه ذلك بنسيم القرنفل وذكر ذلك بعد ذكر المسك نقص

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r4.claim: The phrase about the east wind is syntactically left hanging instead of being joined properly to the first hemistich.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r4.anchor: وقوله نسيم الصبا في تقدير المنقطع عن المصراع الأول لم يصله به وصل مثله

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r5.claim: In the tears passage, “from me” is a weak crutch and filler, while “on the neck” adds nothing because the wet saddle already implies it.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r5.anchor: قوله ففاضت دموع العين ثم استعانته بقوله مني استعانة ضعيفة عند المتأخرين في الصنعة وهو حشو غير مليح

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r6.claim: Repeating the tears in “until my saddle was wet” is needless; “until it wet my saddle” would suffice, and the extra wording pads the meter.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r6.anchor: ثم قوله حتى بل محملي إعادة ذكره الدمع حشو آخر وكان يكفيه أن يقول حتى بلت محملي فاحتاج لإقامة الوزن إلى هذا كله

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r7.claim: Having tears soak the saddle shows excessive effort with a weak result; the poet could have said tears soaked the beloveds’ dwellings, while tears would more plausibly drip onto ground or clothing and would hardly wet a saddle.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r7.anchor: ثم تقديره انه قد أفرط في إفاضة الدمع حتى بل محمله تفريط منه وتقصير ولو كان أبدع لكان يقول حتى بل دمعي مغانيهم وعراصهم

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r8.claim: Bāqillānī says al-Khabzarzī has a better, stronger, more remarkable poem than this line.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r8.anchor: وأنت تجد في شعر الخبزرزي ما هو أحسن من هذا البيت وأمتن وأعجب منه

BAQILLANI:v1p162/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r9.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r9.claim: The second line has neither beauty nor meaning nor striking diction; its ordinary language should not impress readers merely because it names an unfamiliar place.
BAQILLANI:v1p162/r9.anchor: والبيت الثاني خال من المحاسن والبديع خاو من المعنى وليس له لفظ يروق ولا معنى يروع من طباع السوقة

ITQAN:v2p354/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p354/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p354/r2.claim: The phrase means when he dies and falls into the Fire; ʿAdī b. Zayd's use of فتردى witnesses falling.
ITQAN:v2p354/r2.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا تردى ﴾ قال إذا مات وتردى في النار قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r1.claim: Jurjānī rejects the claim that a little grammar improves speech while much grammar spoils it like excess salt, calling that account a distortion without sound analysis.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r1.anchor: القليل من النحو يغنى وان الكثير منه يفسد الكلام كما يفسد الملح الطعام

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r2.claim: For a single clause, a grammatical rule either applies and makes the syntax correct, or does not, leaving the utterance corrupt; there is no intermediate amount to blame.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r2.anchor: لم يخل هذا الحكم من أن يوجد أولا يوجد فإن وجد فقد حصل النحو في الكلام وعدل مزاجه به

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r3.claim: Each sentence in a poem or letter must satisfy grammar on its own; correctness in the first does not repair the second or third, so applying the rule repeatedly is necessary.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r3.anchor: إصلاح الكلام الأول بإجرائه على حكم النحو لا يغنى عنه في الكلام الثاني والثالث

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r4.claim: Grammar is like a balance’s pointer indicating equality: within one clause its correctness cannot meaningfully be excessive or deficient.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r4.anchor: فكما لا يتصور في تلك الصفة زيادة ونقصان حتى يكون كثيرها مذموما وقليلها محمودا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r5.claim: Jurjānī finds Abū Bakr al-Khwārizmī’s dislike of “much inflection” unhelpful: one sentence has no degrees of inflection, while multiple sentences each require their own grammatical correctness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p55/r5.anchor: لا يقع فيه قلة وكثرة إن اعتبرنا الكلام الواحد والجملة الواحدة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p374/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p374/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p374/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses tarda as dying and falling into Hell; he cites a line by Adi ibn Zayd about a man struck by death while expecting a long reign.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p374/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: إذا مات وتردى في النار

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r1.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r1.claim: Ibn al-Athīr glosses the hadith’s “causes him to fall” as bringing a person into ruin.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأثير: أي توقعه في مهلكة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets tarradā as falling into Hell, an Islamic contextual sense supported by the warning immediately afterward and by 37:56 and 41:22.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r2.anchor: وكونه في النار، على تفسير ابن عباس، دلالة إسلامية خاصة لأن ذلك هو المعروف من التردي، كما قال الإمام الطبري

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r3.claim: The author rejects ʿAdī ibn Zayd’s poetic line as evidence for the specifically Islamic sense of falling into Hell; its explicit context points instead to falling to death.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r3.anchor: وأما بيت "عدى بن زيد" فلا يبدو لنا قريباً وجهُ الاستشهاد به على معنى التردى في النار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r3.claim: The inevitable تردّي may be death, ruin, falling into the grave, or falling into Hell; wealth will not help at that point.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r3.anchor: التردي إما أن يكون من الموت أو الهلاك، أو تردى في قبره، أو في نار جهنم فماذا يغني عنه ماله عندها؟

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r4.claim: Because this end is certain, the verse warns against miserliness, oppression, and denying the good; there is no escape from it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r4.anchor: إذن لا مفر منه فلماذا يبخل ويعسر على الآخرين ويطغى ويكذب بالحسنى؟

ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r1.claim: The particle ما may be either a negation or an interrogative particle.
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون ما نافية واستفهامية

ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r2.claim: On the interrogative reading, the verse asks what his wealth could possibly avail him.

ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r3.claim: Mujahid takes تردى from الردى: the person perishes.

ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r4.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r4.claim: Qatada and Abu Salih explain تردى as falling into Hell from its edges.
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح : تردى في جهنم : أي سقط من حافاتها

ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r5.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r5.claim: Some take تردى as being wrapped in the burial shroud, from الردى.
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r5.anchor: وقال قوم : تردى بأكفانه ، من الردى

ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r6.speaker: مالك بن الذئب
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r6.claim: Malik ibn al-Dhayb's line about a spear-struck resting place and cloak supports the shroud sense of تردى.
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r6.anchor: وقال مالك بن الذئب : وخطا بأطراف الأسنة مضجعي *** ورداً على عينيّ فضل ردائيا

ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r7.speaker: آخر
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r7.claim: An unnamed poet says all one's collected wealth leaves only two shrouds and embalming, supporting the burial sense.
ABUHAYYAN:92:11/r7.anchor: وقال آخر : نصيبك مما تجمع الدهر كله *** رداآن تلوي فيهما وحنوط

ALUSI:92:11/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:11/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:11/r1.claim: The opening may be a negative statement, his wealth will not avail him, or an interrogative, what can his wealth avail him?
ALUSI:92:11/r1.anchor: أي ولا يغنى عنه على أن ما نافية أو أي شيء يغنى عنه ماله

ALUSI:92:11/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:11/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI:92:11/r2.anchor: أي هلك تفعل من الردي وهو الهلاك قاله مجاهد

ALUSI:92:11/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:11/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:92:11/r3.claim: Another gloss is falling into the grave pit.

ALUSI:92:11/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:11/r4.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
ALUSI:92:11/r4.claim: Qatāda and Abū Ṣāliḥ say it means falling into Hell.
ALUSI:92:11/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح تردي في جهنم أي سقط

ALUSI:92:11/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:11/r5.speaker: قوم
ALUSI:92:11/r5.claim: Some take taraddā from the shroud, a metaphor for his death and destruction.
ALUSI:92:11/r5.anchor: وقال قوم ترى باكفانه من الرداء وهو كناية عن موته وهلاكه

BAGHAWI:92:11/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:11/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:11/r1.claim: His wealth, which he withheld, will not benefit him when he falls.
BAGHAWI:92:11/r1.anchor: وما يغني عنه ماله }الذي بخل به ،   { إذا تردى

BAGHAWI:92:11/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:11/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI:92:11/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the fall as death.

BAGHAWI:92:11/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:11/r3.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
BAGHAWI:92:11/r3.claim: Qatada and Abu Salih say it means falling into Hell.
BAGHAWI:92:11/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح : هوى في جهنم

BAYDAWI:92:11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:11/r1.claim: The opening may be a plain negation or a rhetorical question rejecting the idea that wealth will help.

BAYDAWI:92:11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:11/r2.claim: Taraddā may mean he perishes, falls into the grave's pit, or plunges into Hell's depths.
BAYDAWI:92:11/r2.anchor: هلك تفعل من الردى أو تردى في حفرة القبر أو قعر جهنم

BIQAI:92:11/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:11/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:11/r1.claim: People of this world escape crises with money, but the wealth this miser withheld in hope of benefit will not help him in that hour.
BIQAI:92:11/r1.anchor: أهل الدنيا إذا وقعوا في ورطة تخلصوا منها بأموالهم

BIQAI:92:11/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:11/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:11/r2.claim: The phrase may be read as an interrogative denial, which negates the wealth's usefulness with greater force.
BIQAI:92:11/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استفهاماً إنكارياً فيكون نافياً للإغناء على أبلغ وجه

BIQAI:92:11/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:11/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:11/r3.claim: Taraddā means perishing by falling into the grave's pit and Hell; the root conveys destruction and falling into a well.
BIQAI:92:11/r3.anchor: أي هلك بالسقوط في حفرة القبر والنار

DURR:92:11/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:11/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:11/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq that “tadarrā” means plunging into the Fire and says the verse concerns Abu Jahl; he cites Adi ibn Zayd's line using the same word of one overtaken by death.
DURR:92:11/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله : { إذا تردى } قال : إذا تردى ودخل في النار نزلت في أبي جهل

DURR:92:11/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:11/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:11/r2.claim: Qatada explains “when he falls” as falling into the Fire.
DURR:92:11/r2.anchor: عن قتادة { إذا تردى } قال : في النار

DURR:92:11/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:11/r3.speaker: author
DURR:92:11/r3.claim: A report cited from Ibn Abi Shayba also glosses the fall as being in the Fire.
DURR:92:11/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة { وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى } قال : في النار

DURR:92:11/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:11/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:92:11/r4.claim: Mujahid explains “when he falls” as when he dies.
DURR:92:11/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : { إذا تردى } قال : إذا مات

IBNASHUR:92:11/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:11/r1.claim: This clause coordinates with the promise of facilitation to al-ʿusrā and means God will hasten him to Hell; the implied phrase is when he falls into it.

IBNASHUR:92:11/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:11/r2.claim: Al-taraddī is falling from a height to a lower place; here the miser's wealth will not avert any of the Fire's punishment.
IBNASHUR:92:11/r2.anchor: لا يغني عنه ماله الذي بخل به شيئا من عذاب النار

IBNASHUR:92:11/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:11/r3.claim: Mā can be negative, yielding the prediction that his wealth will not benefit him when he falls into Hell.
IBNASHUR:92:11/r3.anchor: وسوف لا يغني عنه ماله إذا سقط في جهنم

IBNASHUR:92:11/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:11/r4.claim: Alternatively, mā is an interrogative of rebuke, and on this reading the initial wāw may begin a new sentence: what will his hoarded wealth avail him?
IBNASHUR:92:11/r4.anchor: وهو استفهام إنكار وتوبيخ . ويجوز على هذا الوجه أن تكون الواو للاستئناف

IBNASHUR:92:11/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:92:11/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that a hypocrite took fallen dates from a poor Muslim's children; after the Prophet's offer of a palm in Paradise was refused, Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought the tree for an orchard of forty palms and gave it to the family.
IBNASHUR:92:11/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : « أنه كانت لرجل من المنافقين نخلة مائلة في دار رجل مسلم

IBNASHUR:92:11/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:92:11/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās attributes revelation of Sūrat al-Layl through al-ʿusrā to the story; the report is described as gharīb, and some scholars consequently called the sūra Medinan.
IBNASHUR:92:11/r6.anchor: قال عكرمة قال ابن عباس : فأنزل الله تعالى : { والليل إذا يغشى }

IBNASHUR:92:11/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:11/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cautions that early scholars often used 'revealed concerning this' to mean a story is covered by a verse, not that it occasioned revelation; he applies that convention here.
IBNASHUR:92:11/r7.anchor: وقد بينا في المقدمة الخامسة أنه كثيرا ما يقع في كلام المتقدمين قولهم

IBNASHUR:92:11/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:92:11/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet praised the many luxuriant date clusters awaiting Abū al-Daḥdāḥ in Paradise.
IBNASHUR:92:11/r8.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNASHUR:92:11/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:11/r9.speaker: بشار بن برد
IBNASHUR:92:11/r9.claim: Bashshār ibn Burd alludes to the episode in a line about the little palm bending; al-nuḥayla is the poetic image for the tree.

IBNATIYYA:92:11/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r1.claim: God specifies the moment of the person's ruin as the point when his wealth cannot benefit him, tying the preceding giving and miserliness to wealth.
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r1.anchor: ثم وقف تعالى على موضع غناء ماله عنه وقت ترديه ،   وهذا يدل على أن الإعطاء

IBNATIYYA:92:11/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r2.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r2.claim: Qatāda and Abū Ṣāliḥ say tarradā means falling into Hell, as if falling from its edges.
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r2.anchor: فقال قتادة وأبو صالح معناه { تردى } في جهنم ،   أي سقط من حافاتها

IBNATIYYA:92:11/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r3.claim: Mujāhid understands tarradā as perishing, from the word for ruin.
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد : { تردى } معناه هلك من الردى

IBNATIYYA:92:11/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r4.claim: Some say tarradā means being wrapped in a shroud, citing Mālik ibn al-Rīb's line and another poet's verse as evidence for burial cloth.
IBNATIYYA:92:11/r4.anchor: وقال قوم معناه { تردى } بأكفانه من الرداء ،   ومنه قول مالك بن الربيب

IBNKATHIR:92:11/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:11/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR:92:11/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets the moment of falling as the person's death.

IBNKATHIR:92:11/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:11/r2.speaker: أبو صالح ومالك عن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:11/r2.claim: Abu Salih and Malik, reporting from Zayd ibn Aslam, interpret it as falling into the Fire.
IBNKATHIR:92:11/r2.anchor: وقال أبو صالح ،   ومالك عن زيد بن أسلم : إذا تردى في النار

KASHSHAF:92:11/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:11/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:11/r1.claim: The question “what will avail him?” functions as a denial that anything can benefit him.
KASHSHAF:92:11/r1.anchor: استفهام في معنى الإنكار .   أو نفي

KASHSHAF:92:11/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:11/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:11/r2.claim: Taraddā is derived from radā, to perish, and here means death.
KASHSHAF:92:11/r2.anchor: تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك ،   يريد : الموت

KASHSHAF:92:11/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:11/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:11/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means falling into the grave after burial.
KASHSHAF:92:11/r3.anchor: أو تردى في الحفرة إذا قبر

KASHSHAF:92:11/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:11/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:11/r4.claim: Another possibility is falling into the depths of Hell.

MAWARDI:92:11/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:11/r1.speaker: أبو صالح وزيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI:92:11/r1.claim: The person is unable to use his wealth when he falls into the Fire.
MAWARDI:92:11/r1.anchor: أحدهما : إذا تردى في النار ،   قاله أبو صالح وزيد بن أسلم

MAWARDI:92:11/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:11/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI:92:11/r2.claim: Alternatively, he has died and fallen into his grave.
MAWARDI:92:11/r2.anchor: الثاني : إذا مات فتردى في قبره ،   قاله مجاهد وقتادة

MAWARDI:92:11/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:11/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:11/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests that he has sunk into error and fallen into acts of disobedience.
MAWARDI:92:11/r3.anchor: إذا تردى في ضلاله وهوى في معاصيه

NASAFI:92:11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:11/r1.claim: His wealth will not help him when he perishes.
NASAFI:92:11/r1.anchor: { وَمَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تردى } ولم ينفعه ماله إذا هلك

NASAFI:92:11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:11/r2.claim: Taraddā derives from al-radā, destruction, and can mean he perished.
NASAFI:92:11/r2.anchor: وتردى تفعّل من الردى وهو الهلاك

NASAFI:92:11/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:11/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:11/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means falling into the grave or into the depths of Hell.
NASAFI:92:11/r3.anchor: أو تردى في القبر أو في قعر جهنم أي سقط

QURTUBI:92:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:11/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the phrase can mean when the person dies, perishes, falls into Hell, or goes away; the verb also describes falling into a well or plunging from a mountain.
QURTUBI:92:11/r1.anchor: ويقال : ردي في البئر وتردى : إذا سقط في بئر ، أو تهور من جبل

QURTUBI:92:11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:11/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:11/r2.claim: The particle may be negative: his wealth will not benefit him at all when he perishes.
QURTUBI:92:11/r2.anchor: و " ما " : يحتمل أن تكون جحدا ، أي ولا يغني عنه ماله شيئا

QURTUBI:92:11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:11/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:11/r3.claim: Alternatively, the particle is an interrogative of rebuke: what could his wealth benefit him when he dies and falls into Hell?
QURTUBI:92:11/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون استفهاما معناه التوبيخ ؛ أي أي شيء يغني عنه إذا هلك ووقع في جهنم

RAZI:92:11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:11/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:11/r1.claim: Mā may be an interrogative expressing denial or a simple negation.
RAZI:92:11/r1.anchor: أن ( ما ) هنا يحتمل أن يكون استفهاما بمعنى الإنكار ، ويحتمل أن يكون نفيا

RAZI:92:11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:11/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:11/r2.claim: Taraddā may mean falling from a height, hence falling into the grave or the depths of Hell.
RAZI:92:11/r2.anchor: وأما { تردى } ففيه وجهان ( الأول ) : أن يكون ذلك مأخوذا من قولك : تردى من الجبل : قال الله تعالى : { والمتردية والنطيحة }

RAZI:92:11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:11/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:92:11/r3.claim: The miser's wealth cannot help after he falls into Hell: he left it to his heirs and carried none into the afterlife, where he needs it.
RAZI:92:11/r3.anchor: فماذا يغني عنه ماله الذي بخل به وتركه لوارثه ، ولم يصحبه منه إلى آخرته

RAZI:92:11/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:11/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:92:11/r4.claim: What benefits a person is good sent ahead and wealth spent where due, rather than wealth left to heirs.
RAZI:92:11/r4.anchor: أخبر أن الذي ينتفع الإنسان به هو ما يقدمه الإنسان من أعمال البر وإعطاء الأموال في حقوقها ، دون المال الذي يخلفه على ورثته

RAZI:92:11/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:11/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:92:11/r5.claim: Alternatively, taraddā derives from al-radā, destruction, and means death.
RAZI:92:11/r5.anchor: أن تردى تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك يريد الموت
